name: Inpainting and Canvas Expansion
title: Inpainting and Canvas Expansion
answer: Inpainting and canvas expansion are two related techniques in generative illustration. Inpainting replaces a masked or damaged region inside an image with new content that matches the surrounding style, lighting, and perspective. Canvas expansion, sometimes called outpainting, extends the image beyond its original borders to create a larger composition. Both are used for retouching, object removal, background extension, and adapting artwork to new aspect ratios. They sit within the broader field of visual arts and generative illustration rather than being separate model categories.

sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: These tools run on graphics processing units, either through a hosted cloud service or on a local workstation with a capable GPU. The underlying models are typically diffusion models that hold a compressed representation of the image in memory during generation. A single inpaint or expand operation may require several seconds to a minute depending on resolution and hardware. Many professional workflows use a web interface or a plugin inside an existing image editor, so the heavy computation happens on a remote server.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: The artist first marks the area to be filled or extends the canvas with empty space. The model then looks at the unmasked pixels and any text prompt to infer what should appear in the new region. It repeatedly refines a noisy version of that region until it matches the surrounding context, while keeping the original unmasked pixels largely unchanged. Controls such as mask feathering, prompt strength, and seed value let the artist steer the result. The final step is usually a manual review and light retouching to fix small seams or artifacts.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: The rights in an inpainted or expanded image depend on the tool's terms of service and the source material. If the original image is copyrighted or contains a person's likeness, the edited output may still carry those obligations. Provenance metadata, such as content credentials, is increasingly used to record that a region was generated rather than photographed. The site tracks 92 active intellectual property lawsuits, of which 18 involve AI music services, so image-related disputes are a smaller but still active share. This is a description of current practice, not legal advice.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: Inpainting and canvas expansion are moving toward finer control over lighting, perspective, and material properties. Real-time previews and on-device generation are becoming more common, which reduces the need to send artwork to a cloud service. Video outpainting and 3D canvas expansion are emerging as extensions of the same idea. As models improve, the seam between original and generated pixels will become harder to detect, which also raises the stakes for provenance and disclosure.
